description: Before/after receipts for the Tweedie/NB2 profiling rebuild (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-tweedie-nb-profiling-rebuild-design.md, section 9). 'baseline' is master's code; Task 10 adds 'after'.

provenance.script: benchmarks/tweedie_estimate_p_timing.py, benchmarks/nb_auto_theta_reml.py and the pre-existing benchmarks named under method.commands

method.timing: Three repetitions per case, each a fresh process, cases interleaved with the order reversed on the middle repetition; all seven thread pools pinned to 1; the one-minute load average before each run is recorded. wall_s/cpu_s time the operation only (warmup and data build excluded); peak_rss_mb is the process high-water mark (ru_maxrss), peak_rss_before_operation_mb the same mark just before the operation. reml_search_cost reports its own per-leg wall and sampled peak RSS, and no CPU time.
method.profiling: A separate run: benchmarks/tweedie_estimate_p_timing.py --buckets wraps the functions in BUCKET_TARGETS and charges wall time to the outermost bucket entered (candidate fits: fit_irls_direct, fit_pirls, SuperGLM.fit_reml, the fit_ops publication refits; phi/density: _profile_phi_detailed, _evaluate_tweedie_density, the joint kernel). reml_scale_inside_fits_s is profile_tweedie_reml_scale, timed on its own clock inside candidate fits.

a_series_refusals.question: Does any row need more than 1e6 Dunn-Smyth series terms, or a peak index past 2**52, at the probed (p, phi)?

probe.rows: every positive row of every Tweedie characterisation case (the three re_*.csv files, zeros90, positive96, unpen) and of the private validation dataset
probe.phi: Pearson estimate at the mean refitted at each p, times 1e-3, 0.1, 1, 10, 1e3
probe.terms_needed: 2 sqrt(2 * 37 * mode / (a + 1)), and series_moments(max_terms=1e6) called directly

a_series_refusals.private_validation_dataset: scanned the same way; no refusal; numbers held outside the repository

suite_tweedie_tests.scope: GLM Tweedie/REML-scale/profile tests (20 files), every density, REML-scale and joint-kernel pass instrumented
suite_tweedie_tests.phi_1e-12_is: the pre-rebuild phi search's lower bound (_PHI_LOWER_BOUND), probed by the bounded, branch-scan and fallback machinery the rebuild deletes

a_series_refusals.decision: No probed row exceeds 1e5 terms, let alone 1e6, and no peak index passes 2**52. MAX_ROW_TERMS = 1_000_000 stands and a refusal is an error (FloatingPointError naming p, phi and the row count). Not blocked.
a_series_refusals.flag_for_tasks_3_4: tests/test_tweedie_numerics.py::test_near_perfect_tweedie_fit_does_not_fail_in_fit_statistics fits an exact curve, so the Pearson phi is about 2.6e-26 and the fit-statistics density puts 40 of 40 rows past 2**52; the pre-rebuild code evaluates them by saddlepoint. Under the rebuild's refusal contract that fit raises unless fit statistics handle the refusal. The other off-bound hits are adversarial tests of internals the rebuild deletes.

b_search_fit_mode.question: Is estimate_p(fit_mode='reml', search_fit_mode='fit') at least 1.5x faster than estimate_p(fit_mode='reml')?
b_search_fit_mode.private_validation_dataset: speed-up also at least 1.5x; numbers held outside the repository
b_search_fit_mode.decision: Keep search_fit_mode as it is (spec section 6): the speed-up is at least 1.5x on both the positive96 shape and the private validation dataset, and on the REML search-cost benchmark.

c_p15_bessel_in_fit_reml.question: Is a complete fit_reml at p = 1.5 at least 1.1x faster with the REML-scale Bessel closed form than with the series?
c_p15_bessel_in_fit_reml.mechanism: The Newton phi solve takes its value, score and slope from series_moments; the Bessel methods are reached only from the bounded fallback and its polish, which none of these fits entered (0 calls). The ratios are timing noise around 1.
c_p15_bessel_in_fit_reml.private_validation_dataset: 0 Bessel calls; ratio within noise of 1; numbers held outside the repository
c_p15_bessel_in_fit_reml.decision: Do not keep a Bessel path in fit_reml: it buys nothing (below 1.1x, and never called on the Newton path). The p = 1.5 closed form stays a test oracle only.

d_joint_ml_vs_brent.question: What does removing joint_ml cost on the unpenalized design (informational)?
d_joint_ml_vs_brent.decision: Informational. Removing joint_ml accepts a 2.3x slower estimate_p on unpenalized ML designs at master's phi cost (4 vs 11 candidate fits, p_hat within xatol); Task 10 re-measures Brent with the rebuilt phi solve on this case.

after.method: The baseline was re-measured, not read from 'baseline': a git worktree at 9e0fe6f9 with the Task 1 drivers (commit 4d065875's benchmarks/tweedie_estimate_p_timing.py, nb_auto_theta_reml.py and tweedie_nb_characterisation.py) copied in, and this tree, both run by the same interpreter with PYTHONPATH selecting the tree; superglm.__file__ was checked on every run. Each case ran once per tree per repetition in a fresh pinned process, the trees alternating which went first and the case order reversing on odd repetitions, after one untimed warm-up repetition per tree (numba on-disk caches). Three repetitions for every case; nine for the fixed-p fit_reml, NB, unpen and REML search-cost cases, whose first three medians sat within noise of 1.05. Each tree ran its own copy of every driver. '*_ci' cases time estimate_p(..., ci_alpha=0.05), whose eager interval is part of the call in both trees. unpen_fit on the baseline is master's default method (joint_ml); unpen_fit_brent is master's Brent. reml_search_cost legs run in one process, so their peak RSS is the harness's per-leg VmRSS sample; memory.search_cost_legs_fresh_process has each leg alone.

line_counts.method: wc -l for whole files; the Tweedie part of reml/scale.py is every top-level def/class named *tweedie* with the blank and comment lines above it (619 on master, the spec section 2 figure), and the NB part of model/fit_ops.py every top-level name with an 'nb' token, counted the same way
